claims.text: Vacuum debinding before solid-state sintering will produce a more uniform AlCrFeNiSi microstructure than ambient-air debinding.
Vacuum debinding will reduce compositional segregation in sintered AlCrFeNiSi.
Vacuum debinding will lower residual stresses in sintered AlCrFeNiSi.
Vacuum debinding will reduce processing defects in sintered AlCrFeNiSi.
The microstructural changes caused by vacuum debinding will enhance the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
AlCrFeNiSi powder is prone to segregation and defect formation during ambient-air debinding and sintering.
A temperature range of 1000–1200°C is typical of solid-state sintering for the relevant high-entropy alloys.
Vacuum debinding minimizes oxidation of AlCrFeNiSi powder surfaces relative to ambient-air debinding.
Vacuum debinding promotes more homogeneous binder removal.
Reduced oxidation and homogeneous binder removal lead to more uniform densification during sintering.
Uniform densification produces a finer and more consistent grain structure.
Reduced initial oxide formation and heterogeneity minimize local variations in sintering kinetics.
More uniform sintering kinetics produce a more uniform diffusion process.
A more uniform diffusion process improves grain-boundary cohesion.
Improved grain-boundary cohesion enhances the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi.
Vacuum-debound and sintered AlCrFeNiSi will have greater yield strength than the ambient-air-debound control.
Vacuum-debound and sintered AlCrFeNiSi will have greater toughness than the ambient-air-debound control.
Key mechanical properties may improve by approximately 15–25% following vacuum debinding.
The proposed effects are valid for comparable AlCrFeNiSi feedstocks sintered at 1000–1200°C under hold times that do not induce additional phase changes.
Sintering temperature gradients and vacuum quality may alter the magnitude of the predicted improvements.
